verdict.rationale: vLLM ships the backend surface a coding agent needs: an OpenAI-compatible API server, Anthropic Messages API support, tool calling with auto/required/named tool_choice, and streaming outputs. However, no evidence documents an actual coding agent connected to vLLM end-to-end, or shows how reliably agentic tool loops work against it, so coverage is partial. missing for 10: first-party docs or guides for connecting specific coding agents, hands-on or independent corroboration of coding-agent workflows running on vLLM, documented tool-calling reliability across models in agentic loops.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can connect a coding agent to this product as a working backend

citations.quote: OpenAI-compatible API server, plus Anthropic Messages API and gRPC support
vLLM currently supports named function calling, as well as the `auto`, `required` (as of `vllm>=0.8.3`), and `none` options for the `tool_choice` field in the chat completion API.
Includes a drop-in OpenAI-compatible API for instant integration.
I prefer the OpenAI-Compatible api. Although this is not very technically difficult, it is really intimate, because it make me feel free to use all ChatGPT applications.
